summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would update the Biosecurity Act 2015 to better protect Australia from pests and diseases.
It would let certain legal instruments, like the list of banned goods, refer to documents that can be updated later without rewriting the instrument.
The bill would also clarify the meaning of 'commercial-in-confidence information' and 'human remains', and repeal an outdated fees law from 1985.
changes: Allows instruments under section 174(1) to adopt documents that change over time.
Clarifies definitions for commercial-in-confidence information and human remains.
Improves rules on sharing protected information with National Focal Points under the International Health Regulations.
Fixes technical errors in references and titles.
Repeals the Quarantine (Validation of Fees) Act 1985.
summary.affected: People and businesses involved in biosecurity, including those handling goods or information under the Biosecurity Act.

speeches.speaker: David Littleproud
speeches.brief: The Biosecurity Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Bill 2018 was moved to strengthen Australia's biosecurity system, including new information-gathering powers to track goods like uncooked prawns after import. The Coalition government has increased biosecurity investment by over 29% since 2013, totalling $783.2 million this financial year, with up to $200 million over four years from the Agricultural Competitiveness White Paper.

speeches.speaker: Joel Fitzgibbon
speeches.brief: The opposition will support the Biosecurity Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Bill 2018, citing its expansion of information-gathering powers to allow faster identification of at-risk goods. The member for New England was criticized for abolishing the Inspector-General of Biosecurity in 2015 and the Inspector-General of Animal Welfare and Live Animal Exports, with the latter linked to the Awassi Express incident, and his claim that Labor members hate farmers was disputed.

speeches.speaker: Brian Mitchell
speeches.brief: The member supported the Biosecurity Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Bill 2018, arguing that federal and Tasmanian Liberal governments have under-resourced biosecurity, citing the fruit fly incursion that endangered Tasmania's $50 million stone fruit industry and contrasting Justine Keay's response with former member Brett Whiteley's inaction.

speeches.speaker: David Coleman
speeches.brief: The Biosecurity Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Bill 2018 introduces new information-gathering powers for goods like uncooked prawns released from biosecurity control and establishes a biosecurity imports levy on sea imports from 1 July 2019, projected to raise $325 million. The government has also committed up to $200 million over four years and an additional $121.6 million in the 2018-19 budget to strengthen Australia’s biosecurity system.
